Courses and their module order

Fundamentals to Defence

106 lessons

A broad introduction to security: how systems and networks work, how attackers think, and how defenders protect data and identity.

  1. 1

    Cyber Security Fundamentals

    What security actually is, why it exists, and how defenders think.

    • What Is Cyber Security? →
    • Cybersecurity vs Information Security →
    • The CIA Triad: Confidentiality, Integrity & Availability →
    • Assets, Threats, Vulnerabilities & Risk →
    • Attack Surface & Attack Vectors →
    • Security Controls →
    • The Security Mindset →
  2. 2

    Networking Fundamentals

    How data actually moves — and where a defender can see it.

    • How Data Moves: Packets and the Layered Stack →
    • IP Addressing, Subnetting and NAT →
    • DNS: Turning Names into Addresses →
    • TCP, UDP and the Three-Way Handshake →
    • Ports, Sockets and Common Services →
    • HTTP/HTTPS and the Request–Response Cycle →
    • LANs, Wi-Fi and Wireless Frame Security →
    • Routers, Firewalls and Where Traffic Gets Inspected →
    • VPNs, Proxies and Tunnels →
  3. 3

    Network Attacks and Defences

    How attacks travel across a network, and the defences that stop them.

    • Eavesdropping: Why Traffic Is Readable in the Clear →
    • Man-in-the-Middle, ARP and DNS Spoofing →
    • Denial of Service and Amplification →
    • Password Attacks over the Network: Sniffing, Spraying, Brute Force →
    • Scanning and Enumeration: How a Network Gets Mapped →
    • Malware Delivery over the Network: C2, Beacons and Backdoors →
    • Wireless Attacks: Evil Twin, Deauth and Rogue Access Points →
    • Network Defence: Segmentation, Zero Trust, IDS/IPS →
    • Secure Remote Access in Practice →
  4. 4

    Cryptography Essentials

    What cryptography really guarantees, how it is built, and where it breaks.

    • What Cryptography Actually Promises (and What It Doesn't) →
    • Symmetric Encryption and Key Distribution →
    • Hashing, Salting and Password Storage →
    • Public-Key Cryptography and Key Exchange →
    • Digital Signatures, Certificates and PKI →
    • TLS: How a Secure Connection Is Negotiated →
    • Random Numbers, Nonces and Weak Entropy →
    • Common Crypto Failures and How They Become Real →
    • Key Management: Generate, Store, Rotate, Revoke →
  5. 5

    Operating Systems and the Command Line

    The machine's own rulebook: users, permissions, processes, logs and the shell that drives them.

    • How an OS Is Organised: Kernel, Users, Files, Permissions →
    • Windows Security Model: Tokens, UAC and Active Directory Basics →
    • Linux Permissions, Users and Groups →
    • The Command Line for Security Work →
    • Processes, Services and Persistence Mechanisms →
    • Logs: Where the OS Tells You What Happened →
    • Patching, Updates and Vulnerability Management →
    • Endpoint Protection: AV, EDR and Application Control →
    • Hardening a Fresh Install (CIS-style Baselines) →

    Identity, Authentication and Access Control

    Who are you, what did you prove, and what may you actually do?

    • Accounts, Identifiers and Why Identity Is the New Perimeter →
    • Passwords: Creation, Storage and Rotation Reality →
    • Multi-Factor Authentication and Passkeys →
    • Session Management and Account Takeover →
    • Authorisation vs Authentication: Least Privilege in Practice →
    • Directory Services, SSO and Federation →
    • Privilege Escalation and Admin Account Hygiene →
    • Service Accounts, API Keys and Secrets Management →
    • Access Reviews, Joiner–Mover–Leaver and Deprovisioning →

    Data Protection and Endpoint Security

    • Data Classification: What You Actually Need to Protect →
    • Encryption at Rest, in Transit and in Backup →
